title: Communicate to Play: Pragmatic Reasoning for Efficient Cross-Cultural Communication in Codenames

bias_targets.methodology: Training word embeddings and prompting LLMs on cultural subsets of the Cultural Codes dataset to measure alignment with human gameplay and evaluate cross-cultural pragmatic failures in Codenames Duet.
Comparing guess and target accuracy of models simulating players with different educational backgrounds (high school/associate vs. bachelor vs. master/doctorate).
Evaluating model alignment and guess accuracy against human Codenames players split by political leanings (liberal vs. conservative).
Measuring discrepancies in guess and target selection accuracy for models representing different age groups (under 30 vs. 30 or above).
Comparing model performance and semantic associations between simulated Catholic and non-Catholic players.
Evaluating gameplay alignment and target accuracy of models trained on data from players from the United States versus foreign countries.
Comparing accuracy differences in word association and target selection between simulated native and non-native English speakers.
Comparing guess and target accuracy using word embeddings trained separately on male versus female player data.
